title: Factors and Impacts of Major Selection on Mechanical Engineering Students in Vocational High School
text_snippet: Factors and Impacts of Major Selection on Mechanical Engineering Students in Vocational High School The phenomenon of mismatch between the chosen major and students’ interests in vocational education has become an important issue because it has the potential to affect the learning process and students’ psychological conditions. This study aims to examine the factors that influence the selection of majors as well as their impact on students’ learning engagement and psychological conditions. This research uses a descriptive qualitative approach with a case study design. The research subjects consist of eleventh-grade students of the Mechanical Engineering major selected purposively, as well as supporting informants, namely guidance and counseling teachers and the head of the major. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation using interview guidelines as the main instrument. Data analysis was conducted using an interactive model through the stages of data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing with triangulation techniques to ensure data validity. title: An Economics Pocket Book on Financial Literacy for Tenth Grade Students
text_snippet: An Economics Pocket Book on Financial Literacy for Tenth Grade Students The availability of relevant, practical, and easy-to-understand teaching materials is an important requirement in supporting the learning process, especially in financial literacy material. The main problem in this study is the unavailability of concise teaching materials that can help 10th grade students understand the basic concepts of personal financial management in a simple and applicable manner. This study aims to develop, validate, and produce a financial literacy pocketbook that is suitable for use as a medium for economics learning. This type of research is Research and Development (R&D) using the ADDIE model. The research subjects included material experts, media experts, economics teachers, and 10th grade students. Research data were obtained through validation sheets, teacher response questionnaires, and trials with students. The developed pocketbook contains basic financial literacy materials, such as money management, needs and wants, priority scales, saving, and simple financial decision-making. title: Student Perceptions of the Role of Microteaching Courses as Preparation for Implementing Field Experience Practices
text_snippet: Student Perceptions of the Role of Microteaching Courses as Preparation for Implementing Field Experience Practices Microteaching is widely implemented as a preparatory course prior to Field Experience Practice (FEP); however, its effectiveness in representing the complexity of authentic classroom instruction remains contested. This study aims to analyze students’ perceptions of microteaching as preparation for FEP and examine the relationship between students’ perceptions and their academic achievement in the microteaching course. A convergent mixed-methods design was employed involving 35 undergraduate students enrolled in a Japanese Language Education program. Data were collected through an online questionnaire consisting of students’ perceptions of microteaching and documentation of final course grades. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, normality testing, and correlation analysis, while qualitative data were analyzed through thematic analysis. The findings revealed that students generally perceived microteaching positively, particularly in enhancing self-confidence, teaching readiness, and adaptability to student characteristics. Nevertheless, no significant relationship was identified between students’ perceptions and their academic achievement in microteaching.

title: Prophetic Food Program: Integrating Islamic Values and Local Food Literacy to Develop Moral Character in Elementary Students
text_snippet: Prophetic Food Program: Integrating Islamic Values and Local Food Literacy to Develop Moral Character in Elementary Students The low level of local food literacy and the weak development of moral character among elementary school students remain critical problems due to the dominance of instant food consumption and the limited integration of value-based education. These conditions negatively affect students’ nutritional awareness, hygiene, justice, and ethical eating behavior. This study aimed to develop and examine the effectiveness of the Prophetic Food Program in enhancing students’ local food literacy and moral character. A mixed-methods approach with a sequential exploratory design was employed. The research subjects consisted of 70 fifth-grade students as experimental participants, as well as 140 students and 14 teachers as perception survey respondents. Data were collected through tests, questionnaires, observations, interviews, and documentation. Data analysis applied qualitative thematic analysis and quantitative paired t-test and N-Gain analysis. The findings indicate that the program significantly improves students’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward local food as well as the internalization of prophetic values (al-‘adl, al-ṭahārah, al-qanā'ah, al-karīm, and al-akhlāq al-karīmah) with

title: Orchestrating Research Culture: Principal's Strategic Planning in Institutionalizing Mandatory Youth Scientific Work Literacy
text_snippet: Orchestrating Research Culture: Principal's Strategic Planning in Institutionalizing Mandatory Youth Scientific Work Literacy This study is driven by the urgency to transform scientific activities in schools from extracurricular practices into an institutionalized academic culture. The study aims to analyze the principal’s strategic planning in institutionalizing the Youth Scientific Work (KIR) literacy program as a mandatory academic requirement. This research employs a qualitative approach with a case study method. The subjects of the study include the principal, teachers, and students involved in the KIR program. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, participant observation, and documentation studies using interview guidelines, observation sheets, and document analysis instruments. Data validity was ensured through source and technique triangulation. Data analysis was conducted using the interactive model by Miles and Huberman, including data collection, condensation, display, and conclusion drawing. title: A Critical Analysis of Pre-Service Islamic Elementary Teachers’Problem-Solving Abilities in Science Education
text_snippet: A Critical Analysis of Pre-Service Islamic Elementary Teachers’Problem-Solving Abilities in Science Education The low problem-solving skills of prospective teacher students pose a challenge in preparing educators capable of designing meaningful and contextual science learning. This ability is important because prospective teachers are required to have critical, analytical, and reflective thinking skills in dealing with various learning problems in elementary schools. This study aims to critically analyze the problem-solving abilities of PGMI students in the context of science learning. The study used a descriptive quantitative approach involving 36 sixth-semester PGMI students selected through a purposive sampling technique. Data collection was conducted using a case study-based test developed based on six problem-solving indicators, including defining the problem, diagnosing the problem, formulating alternative strategies, selecting and implementing strategies, evaluating implementation, and determining the implications of science learning. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics through percentage calculations and distribution of ability categories. title: Integrated E-Module of Local Potential Mount Merbabu to Improve High School Students Sustainable Development Goals Literacy
text_snippet: Integrated E-Module of Local Potential Mount Merbabu to Improve High School Students Sustainable Development Goals Literacy Literacy regarding the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly Goal 15 (Life on Land), remains relatively low due to a lack of integration of literacy into learning and a scarcity of innovative learning resources. This situation calls for the development of teaching materials that are contextual and relevant to the students’ surrounding environment. This study aims to analyze, develop, and test the validity, practicality, and effectiveness of an e-module based on local potential as a tool for SDG literacy learning. This is a development study using the 4D model (Define, Design, Develop, Disseminate) involving teachers and students as research subjects. Data were collected through interviews, questionnaires, and tests, using instruments tailored to the aspects being measured. Qualitative data were analyzed using the Miles and Huberman technique, while quantitative data were analyzed using percentage and n-gain calculations. The research results indicate that the developed e-module has a very high level of validity based on expert evaluation and is considered highly practical in its application. title: Virtual Reality Integrated ew TPACK and PBL to Improve Critical Thinking Ability in Science Learning for Elementary School
text_snippet: Virtual Reality Integrated ew TPACK and PBL to Improve Critical Thinking Ability in Science Learning for Elementary School The gap in science learning in elementary schools remains a problem that impacts students' low critical thinking skills and scientific literacy, mainly due to teachers' limitations in preparing interactive learning media integrated with innovative learning models. This study aims to develop interactive media with Virtual Reality (VR) based on TPACK-PBL in science learning to improve critical thinking skills and scientific literacy of sixth grade elementary school students. This study uses the Research and Development (R&D) method with the ADDIE development model. The research subjects consisted of 15 students in the trial class and 20 students in the effectiveness test class. Quantitative data were obtained through validation by material, language, and graphics experts, product trials, and effectiveness tests using pretests and posttests, while qualitative data were obtained through interviews, observations, and questionnaires of teacher and student responses. The results of the study indicate that interactive media with VR based on TPACK-PBL is effective in improving students' critical thinking skills and scientific literacy. title: Implication of Role Playing Techniques in Group Guidance to Address Bullying Issues among Students
text_snippet: Implication of Role Playing Techniques in Group Guidance to Address Bullying Issues among Students Bullying in schools is a socio-psychological problem that has a significant impact on the emotional, academic, and moral development of students. This phenomenon is still found at MA Al Iman Adiwerna, especially in the form of verbal bullying and mild physical violence, which are often considered jokes. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of role-playing techniques in group guidance services to address bullying behavior among students in class X-1. The study uses a qualitative approach with a case study design, involving 11 participants consisting of the principal, guidance and counseling teachers, and students. Data collection was conducted through interviews, observations, and documentation, then analyzed using the Miles and Huberman model. The results showed that the application of role-playing techniques was effective in increasing students' awareness of the impact of bullying, improving interpersonal communication, and fostering empathy and emotional sensitivity. The experience of playing the roles of perpetrator, victim, and witness helped students understand the emotional and moral consequences of bullying behavior. title: The Influence of the GASING Method on Basic Multiplication Concept Understanding in Third Grade Elementary School Students
text_snippet: The Influence of the GASING Method on Basic Multiplication Concept Understanding in Third Grade Elementary School Students The low level of understanding of basic multiplication concepts among elementary school students remains a recurring educational challenge in Indonesia. This study aims to examine the effect of the GASING (Easy, Fun, Enjoyable) method on third-grade students’ understanding of basic multiplication concepts. The study employed a quasi-experimental design with a nonequivalent control group, involving students from two schools selected through purposive sampling. The experimental class received instruction using the GASING method through structured stages, namely concrete, abstract, and mental calculation, while the control class received conventional instruction. Data were collected through essay tests and analyzed using N-Gain scores, t-tests, and Cohen’s d effect size. The results indicate that the experimental class achieved a significantly higher improvement in learning outcomes compared to the control class, with a high level of improvement and a large effect size. title: Transformational Leadership and Achievement Motivation as Predictors of Teacher Performance
text_snippet: Transformational Leadership and Achievement Motivation as Predictors of Teacher Performance Teacher performance is a crucial factor in determining the quality of learning, but problems remain, including suboptimal principal leadership and teacher achievement motivation, which impact performance achievement. This study aims to analyze the influence of transformational leadership and achievement motivation on teacher performance at a senior high school (SMAN). The study employed a quantitative approach with a correlational design. The study population consisted of 40 teachers, all of whom served as respondents. Data were collected through a questionnaire that had been tested for validity and reliability, then analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression. The results showed that transformational leadership and achievement motivation had a positive and significant effect on teacher performance, both partially and simultaneously. Both variables contributed significantly to explaining variations in teacher performance. This finding indicates that improving teacher performance requires a synergy between effective transformational leadership and strengthening achievement motivation. title: Exploring Speaking Anxiety in English Language Learning: Causes and Coping Strategies among University Students
text_snippet: Exploring Speaking Anxiety in English Language Learning: Causes and Coping Strategies among University Students Speaking anxiety in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning remains a challenge that affects students’ communicative performance, while integrated studies linking its causes and coping strategies are still limited. This study aims to analyze the determinants of speaking anxiety and evaluate the coping strategies employed by second-year university students. Using a qualitative case study design, six purposively selected participants were involved. Data were collected through in-depth interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings indicate that speaking anxiety is influenced by fear of making mistakes, limited vocabulary, and insufficient preparation, which affect students’ confidence and fluency. To manage these challenges, participants employed strategies such as preparation, relaxation, positive thinking, peer support, and acceptance. The results highlight that while preparation is important, positive thinking plays a more dominant role in alleviating anxiety. title: Google Sites–Assisted Interactive Learning Multimedia to Enhance Learning Motivation and Cognitive Learning Outcomes in Social Studies among Elementary School
text_snippet: Google Sites–Assisted Interactive Learning Multimedia to Enhance Learning Motivation and Cognitive Learning Outcomes in Social Studies among Elementary School The low motivation and learning outcomes of social studies in elementary school students indicate that the use of learning media is still not fully capable of creating an interactive, contextual, and student-centered learning experience. This condition indicates the need for digital learning media innovations that can increase student engagement more optimally in the learning process. This study aims to develop, evaluate, and test the effectiveness of interactive learning multimedia assisted by Google Sites in improving the motivation and cognitive learning outcomes of fifth-grade elementary school students. This study uses a Research and Development (R&D) approach with the Borg and Gall model. The research subjects included material experts, media experts, teachers, and elementary school students. Data were collected through interviews, observations, questionnaires, and cognitive learning outcome tests, then analyzed using quantitative descriptive and inferential techniques to interpret the level of validity, practicality, and effectiveness of the developed product. title: The Impact of Immersive Learning Assisted by Virtual Reality and Automated Writing Evaluation on Writing Skills and Higher-Order Thinking Skills
text_snippet: The Impact of Immersive Learning Assisted by Virtual Reality and Automated Writing Evaluation on Writing Skills and Higher-Order Thinking Skills Most high school students still struggle with writing observational texts, particularly when it comes to describing objects in detail, critically, and creatively. This study aims to examine the impact of immersive learning supported by augmented reality (AR) and automated writing evaluation (AWE) on students’ writing skills and higher-order thinking skills. This study used a quasi-experimental method involving 250 high school students divided into an experimental group and a control group. The experimental group received AR- and AWE-assisted immersive learning, while the control group received conventional instruction. Data collection was conducted using a writing skills assessment rubric, a higher-order thinking skills questionnaire, and feedback coding. Data were analyzed using ANCOVA, the Chi-square test, and mediation analysis.The results of the study indicate that AR- and AWE-assisted immersive learning has a significant impact on improving writing skills and higher-order thinking skills compared to conventional learning. title: Moral Integrity of Pandita Magabudhi in Promoting Religious Moderation
text_snippet: Moral Integrity of Pandita Magabudhi in Promoting Religious Moderation In Indonesia’s multicultural society, frictions and conflicts among religious communities persist due to the emergence of extremist interpretations of religion. In this context, this study aims to comprehensively examine the dynamics of the Buddhist Religious Institution of the Indonesian Theravada Buddhist Council (MAGABUDHI). This research employs an interpretative qualitative approach, presented through descriptive and interpretative analysis. Primary data were obtained from key informants, consisting of the Chairperson of the Regional Board of MAGABUDHI, six religious leaders, and six members of MAGABUDHI. Secondary data were derived from relevant literature. Data were collected through observation, in-depth interviews, and document analysis. The research instruments included interview guidelines, audio recording devices, and visual recording tools. Data analysis was conducted using qualitative descriptive techniques, encompassing data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings reveal three main aspects. title: Discovery Learning–Based Worksheets Integrating Flood Disaster Literacy to Enhance Collaboration and Creativity in Elementary School
text_snippet: Discovery Learning–Based Worksheets Integrating Flood Disaster Literacy to Enhance Collaboration and Creativity in Elementary School Science learning on the topic of ecosystems in elementary schools still faces various problems, such as low student engagement, limited contextual teaching materials, and less than optimal development of collaboration and creativity skills. The flood-prone environment of students demands learning that integrates disaster literacy with ecosystem concepts through active and meaningful activities. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of Student Worksheets (LKPD) based on the Discovery Learning model containing flood disaster literacy on the topic of ecosystems in improving collaboration and creativity skills of elementary school students. This study is a research and development (R&D) using the ADDIE model. The research subjects consisted of fifth-grade students selected using purposive sampling techniques. Data were collected through expert validation, observation, testing, and documentation, then analyzed using validity analysis techniques and analysis of learning outcomes improvement. title: A Synergistic STEM-Creativity Model to Enhance Cognitive Innovation and Higher-Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) in Mathematics Learning
text_snippet: A Synergistic STEM-Creativity Model to Enhance Cognitive Innovation and Higher-Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) in Mathematics Learning Students’ low levels of cognitive innovation and higher-order thinking skills (HOTS) in mathematics learning remain a major problem caused by teacher-centered instruction and a lack of contextual problem-solving activities. This study aims to analyze and test the effectiveness of the Synergistic STEM–Creativity Learning Model in improving students’ cognitive innovation and HOTS in mathematics learning. This study employs a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control group design. The research participants consisted of 68 junior high school students divided into an experimental class and a control class. Data collection was conducted through HOTS essay tests and Likert scale questionnaires to measure students’ cognitive innovation abilities. The data were analyzed using assumption tests, hypothesis tests, and N-Gain to evaluate the improvement in abilities and differences in learning outcomes between groups. The results of the study indicate that students in the experimental class demonstrated a greater improvement in cognitive innovation and higher-order thinking skills (HOTS) compared to students in the control class. title: Readiness of Science Education Teachers for Online Teaching Internship
text_snippet: Readiness of Science Education Teachers for Online Teaching Internship The development of online and hybrid learning poses new challenges for teacher education programs in preparing prospective Science teachers for virtual teaching practice. This study aims to analyze the readiness of fourth-year Science education students for online teaching internships based on their technological, academic, and pedagogical competencies. This study used a mixed-methods approach with a sequential explanatory design. The study subjects consisted of 63 Science education students. Data were collected through questionnaires, achievement tests, and semi-structured interviews using instruments such as readiness questionnaires, academic ability tests, and interview guidelines. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and thematic analysis. The results showed that students had good technological competencies, consistent academic achievement in core science domains, and pedagogical readiness in lesson planning, implementation of learning strategies, classroom management, and online assessment. title: Measuring English Teachers' Digital Literacy in Applying ICT: A Study in a Secondary School
text_snippet: Measuring English Teachers' Digital Literacy in Applying ICT: A Study in a Secondary School The development of digital technology in education requires teachers to have adequate digital literacy to support effective and innovative English language learning. However, the digital competence of English teachers in secondary schools still shows inequality, especially in the pedagogical integration of ICT, digital assessment, and technology-based professional development. This study aims to analyze, evaluate, and interpret the level of digital literacy of English teachers in the application of ICT based on the Digital Competence for Language Teachers DC4LT framework. This study used a mixed methods method with an explanatory sequential design. The research subjects consisted of 36 secondary school English teachers, while the instrument trial subjects involved 15 teachers outside the research sample. Data collection was carried out through questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, and documentation using instruments in the form of a validated DC4LT questionnaire and interview guide. title: Bibliometric Evaluation of Scientific Journals: An Overview for Strengthening Scientific Journal Accreditation
text_snippet: Bibliometric Evaluation of Scientific Journals: An Overview for Strengthening Scientific Journal Accreditation Scientific journal evaluation plays a crucial role in ensuring the quality and credibility of scientific publications. However, research mapping journal evaluation as a basis for strengthening journal accreditation is currently limited. This study aims to identify global research patterns, trends, and dynamics related to scientific journal evaluation to support the development of journal accreditation policies in Indonesia. This study used a bibliometric approach to 336 Scopus-indexed publications. Data were collected through a Scopus database search using relevant keywords as research instruments. The data were analyzed using bibliometric analysis, including publication performance, keyword co-occurrence, co-citation, and collaboration networks. The results show that journal evaluation studies have evolved from traditional bibliometric indicators, such as impact factor and citation analysis, to a multidimensional approach that emphasizes transparency, publication ethics, and open access. title: Mapping HOTS in Textbook Assessment Items: Implications for Instructional and Learning Quality
text_snippet: Mapping HOTS in Textbook Assessment Items: Implications for Instructional and Learning Quality The main problem in Indonesian language learning at the high school level is the low application of Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) aspects in evaluation questions, which impacts the development of students' critical, analytical, and creative thinking abilities. This study is motivated by the need to improve the quality of learning thru assessments that demand higher-order thinking skills. This study aims to analyze and evaluate the representation of HOTS aspects in the evaluation questions within the Tiga Serangkai Indonesian Language textbook for SMA Class X, and to assess its implications for the quality of learning. The research subject is the evaluation questions in the Indonesian textbook "Tiga Serangkai" for high school students in Class X, with a total of 60 questions analyzed. Data collection was carried out using the content analysis method, with the instrument being a categorization sheet based on the revised Bloom's taxonomy (C4–C6). Data analysis techniques included identifying, classifying, and interpreting the cognitive levels of the evaluation questions. title: Strengthening Leadership Communication Based on Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP) for Teachers and School Principals
text_snippet: Strengthening Leadership Communication Based on Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP) for Teachers and School Principals Despite the critical role of leadership communication in educational transformation, many teachers and principals still experience limitations in empathetic and strategic communication, resulting in suboptimal collaboration and innovation. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP)-based training in enhancing leadership communication competencies among educational practitioners. The research employed a quasi-experimental design with a pre-test–post-test approach involving 39 participants, including teachers, school leaders, and postgraduate students. Data were collected using validated instruments measuring authentic leadership, NLP-based communication skills, and teacher performance, supported by reflective writings and peer feedback. Quantitative data were analyzed using paired-samples t-tests, while qualitative data were examined through thematic analysis. The results indicate a significant improvement in participants’ communication competencies across cognitive, behavioral, and affective domains. title: PAK ADI Based Small Ball Game Development Model to Improve Physical Learning In Elementary Schools
text_snippet: PAK ADI Based Small Ball Game Development Model to Improve Physical Learning In Elementary Schools Elementary school students' small-ball game skills have not yet developed optimally because physical education instruction remains predominantly teacher-centered and has not adopted innovative learning models. This study aimed to analyze the effectiveness of the PAK ADI learning model (Participatory, Analytical, Creative, Active, Demonstrative, and Innovative) in improving elementary school students' small-ball game skills. This study employed a Research and Development (R&D) method based on the Borg and Gall model, consisting of the stages of preliminary research, planning, validation, evaluation and revision, and model implementation. The research participants included subject-matter experts, instructional experts, physical education teachers, and elementary school students involved in both small-group and large-group trials. Data were collected through classroom observations, validation questionnaires, user response questionnaires, and small-ball game skills tests. The research instruments consisted of expert validation sheets, observation sheets, practicality questionnaires, and learning outcome tests. title: The Writerpreneur E-Platform Based on a Metacognitive Approach in Improving Essay Writing Competence and Digital Literacy Entrepreneurship
text_snippet: The Writerpreneur E-Platform Based on a Metacognitive Approach in Improving Essay Writing Competence and Digital Literacy Entrepreneurship The problem of this research lies in the suboptimal utilization of students' writing skills in the field of digital literacy entrepreneurship and the still low self-regulation and metacognitive abilities in the essay writing process. Writing learning in higher education still focuses on the final result, so that the process of planning, monitoring, and evaluation of writing has not been developed optimally. This study aims to analyze, evaluate, and test the effectiveness of the writerpreneur e-platform based on a metacognitive approach in improving students' essay writing and digital literacy entrepreneurship competencies. This study used a quasi-experimental research type with a nonequivalent control group design. The research subjects were 250 students and who were divided into experimental and control groups of 125 students each. Data collection methods were carried out through essay writing tests, digital entrepreneurship questionnaires, observations, and interviews using writing assessment rubrics, Likert scales, and interview guidelines. In addition, the New Student Admission System (SPMB) process is not yet digitally integrated, resulting in less effective information dissemination, registration processes, and student data management. This study aims to analyze, develop, and evaluate the design and implementation of omnichannel E-SPMB as a digital channel integration strategy to support the effectiveness of SPMB. This study uses the Research and Development (R&D) method with the ADDIE model development design. The research subjects consisted of 2 expert validators, namely 1 material expert and 1 media expert, as well as trial subjects involving 1 school principal and 1 SPMB team leader. Data were collected through observation, interviews, expert validation questionnaires, and user response questionnaires using observation guidelines, interview guidelines, and questionnaire sheets. title: Project-Based STEAM Learning Model in Science Education to Enhance Elementary School Students’ Creative Thinking Skills
text_snippet: Project-Based STEAM Learning Model in Science Education to Enhance Elementary School Students’ Creative Thinking Skills The low creative thinking ability of elementary school students remains a problem in science learning. In addition, the learning model used has not fully encouraged the integration of 21st-century skills such as creativity and problem-solving. This study aims to analyze the STEAM-based Project-Based Learning (STEAM-PjBL) learning model to improve students' creative thinking abilities. This type of research is Research and Development (R&D) with the ADDIE development design. The research subjects consisted of 45 fifth-grade students. Data collection was carried out through validation sheets from material experts and model experts, teacher and student response questionnaires, and creative thinking ability tests through pretests and posttests. Data analysis used descriptive and inferential methods, including paired samples t-tests. The results of the study indicate that the developed STEAM-PjBL model is in the very valid category, received very positive responses from teachers and students, and has proven effective in improving students' creative thinking abilities. title: Improving Students’ Communication Skills: A Literature Review on the Effectiveness of Teams Games Tournament-Based Learning
text_snippet: Improving Students’ Communication Skills: A Literature Review on the Effectiveness of Teams Games Tournament-Based Learning Communication skills are one of the key competencies needed in the workplace, but educational institutions have not been able to optimally develop these skills in students. The use of conventional learning methods that are still dominant results in low student participation and interaction in the learning process. This study aims to analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the Teams Games Tournament (TGT) cooperative learning model in improving students' communication skills. This study uses a qualitative approach with a literature review design. The research subjects consisted of 25 scientific articles relevant to the TGT model and communication skills, which were selected based on inclusion criteria. The data collection method used documentation techniques with instruments in the form of document analysis sheets compiled based on communication skills indicators. Instrument validity was carried out through content validity testing and source triangulation. title: The Impact of LuDiCa Program with a Phonic Approach on the Language and Literacy Skills of Early Childhood Students
text_snippet: The Impact of LuDiCa Program with a Phonic Approach on the Language and Literacy Skills of Early Childhood Students Many students entering early primary school are still unable to read due to limited literacy activities during the preschool years. This study aims to analyze the impact of the Dialogic Reading for Comprehension (LuDiCa) intervention program, using a phonics-based approach, on the development of young learners’ language and literacy skills. A quasi experimental research design was employed to examine the effectiveness of the dialogic reading program. The research subjects consisted of 250 young children and their parents who participated in the study. Participants were randomly selected from several early childhood education institutions. The instruments used in this study included questionnaires, language and literacy assessments, receptive and expressive vocabulary assessments, taxonomy skills assessments, print awareness assessments, and activity sheets. Data were analyzed using a hierarchical linear model with a two level random intercept. The findings indicate that the phonics-based Dialogic Reading for Comprehension (LuDiCa) program is effective in improving students’ reading and literacy skills. title: Impact of Writing Learning Model Flipped Classroom Based on Video on the Writing Ability and Quality of Procedural Text Components
text_snippet: Impact of Writing Learning Model Flipped Classroom Based on Video on the Writing Ability and Quality of Procedural Text Components This study was motivated by the majority of junior high school students who were still having difficulty writing procedure text. The purpose of this study is to test the impact of video -based class learning models on the ability to write and the quality of procedure text components. The method used is quasi-experimental involving 250 junior high school students with each group of 125 students. Data analysis using nonparametric tests, namely Mann-Whitney and Wilcoxon Signed Rank Tests. title: The Islamic Religious Education Teacher Performance Assessment Model Eksplorasi Model Penilaian Kinerja Guru Pendidikan Agama Islam di Sekolah Menengah Atas di Jawa Barat
text_snippet: The Islamic Religious Education Teacher Performance Assessment Model Eksplorasi Model Penilaian Kinerja Guru Pendidikan Agama Islam di Sekolah Menengah Atas di Jawa Barat Teacher performance assessment that has been implemented so far often focuses primarily on administrative or technical aspects, and therefore does not fully reflect the actual quality of the learning process. This study aims to explore the implementation and the need for developing a performance assessment model for Islamic Religious Education (PAI) teachers at the senior high school level. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, field observations, and document analysis. Informants were selected purposively, consisting of PAI teachers, school principals, and PAI supervisors. The data were analyzed using the interactive analysis model proposed by Miles and Huberman. The findings reveal that the existing teacher performance assessment model remains largely administrative in nature and does not adequately incorporate aspects such as personality, spirituality, and the exemplary character expected of PAI teachers. These findings indicate the need to develop a more holistic and contextual assessment model to measure teachers’ contributions to character formation and the internalization of Islamic values among students. title: Language Variety Use in the Learning Process of Indonesian Language for Junior High School Students
text_snippet: Language Variety Use in the Learning Process of Indonesian Language for Junior High School Students This study is motivated by the suboptimal management of language variety use in Indonesian language instruction, which may affect communication effectiveness and students’ academic language mastery. Language variation naturally occurs in classroom interaction however, it is not always pedagogically managed to support instructional objectives. This study aims to analyze the use of language varieties in Indonesian language learning at the junior high school level using a mixed method approach. The quantitative approach was employed to identify the frequency and percentage of language variety use through structured observation and questionnaires, which were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Meanwhile, the qualitative approach was applied to describe the forms and contexts of language use through note taking techniques, participant observation, interviews, and documentation, which were analyzed using an interactive analysis model. The data were derived from teachers’ and students’ utterances during classroom instruction. title: Improving Writing Creativity and Creative Thinking Through Collaborative Guided Writing Strategies Assisted by Gen-AI and Multimedia
text_snippet: Improving Writing Creativity and Creative Thinking Through Collaborative Guided Writing Strategies Assisted by Gen-AI and Multimedia The majority of high school students still experience difficulties in creative thinking and creative writing. This study aims to investigate the impact of a guided writing strategy based on Gen-AI and multimedia on creative writing skills and creative thinking abilities. The research method used in this study was a quasi-experimental study involving 250 high school students. Data collection methods used the Torrance Creative Thinking Test and a writing creativity scale. The results showed that a guided writing strategy based on Gen-AI and multimedia improved creative thinking skills and writing creativity in short story writing. Increased flexibility was seen in language variations and adaptation of short stories to short story composition topics. Increased originality was seen in students' thought patterns in the short stories they wrote. Increased elaboration was characterized by more complex and varied linguistic abilities. Furthermore, increased sensitivity was seen in the adaptation of short stories to more comprehensive themes. title: The Contextual Problem-Based Learning Model Enhances Problem-Solving Abilities and Science Process Skills Among Elementary School Students
text_snippet: The Contextual Problem-Based Learning Model Enhances Problem-Solving Abilities and Science Process Skills Among Elementary School Students Science learning in elementary schools often emphasizes the theoretical delivery of concepts, which has not optimally fostered students’ critical thinking and scientific skills. This study aims to analyze the effect of contextual Problem-Based Learning on elementary school students’ problem-solving abilities and scientific process skills in science learning. This study employed a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design, as full randomization of classes was not feasible in the natural school setting. The research participants consisted of fifth-grade students from two public elementary schools, which were assigned as the experimental and control groups. Data were collected through problem-solving ability tests and scientific process skills tests. The data were analyzed using the Analysis of Covariance to control for differences in students’ initial abilities. The results indicate that contextual problem-based learning exerts a very strong effect on improving students’ problem-solving abilities after controlling for their initial competence. title: Social Support as a Predictor of Positive Peer Relationships in Boarding School Students
text_snippet: Social Support as a Predictor of Positive Peer Relationships in Boarding School Students Learning in a boarding school environment presents unique challenges due to academic demands and responsibilities that may influence the quality of peer relationships. This condition raises questions regarding the extent to which social support contributes to the development of positive peer relationships. This study aims to examine the effect of social support on positive peer relationships among boarding school students. This study employed a quantitative approach using a survey design. The research instruments consisted of psychological scales that had undergone content and construct validity testing, as well as reliability testing using Cronbach’s Alpha. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to respondents and subsequently analyzed using SmartPLS 3 through the PLS algorithm, bootstrapping, and PLSPredict procedures. The results indicate that social support plays a significant role in predicting positive peer relationships, with an effective contribution of 21.1%. Social support also significantly influences the dimensions of intimacy, popularity, trust, and insight within peer relationships. The research subjects consisted of 30 eleventh-grade students from the Motorcycle Engineering (TBSM) program, with 10 students selected purposively for the limited trial phase. title: The Influence of Financial Knowledge, Positive Emotions, and Store Atmosphere on College Students' Impulsive Buying
text_snippet: The Influence of Financial Knowledge, Positive Emotions, and Store Atmosphere on College Students' Impulsive Buying Impulse buying refers to spontaneous purchasing behavior that occurs without prior planning and is often influenced by emotional and environmental factors. This study aims to analyze the effects of financial knowledge, positive emotions, and store atmosphere on impulse buying behavior among university students. This research employed a descriptive quantitative approach and was grounded in Social Cognitive Theory, which posits that behavior results from the interaction between personal, behavioral, and environmental factors. The sample consisted of 268 students from the Economic Education study program who were selected using a proportionate random sampling technique and had completed at least one course related to finance. Data were collected through a closed-ended questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression after passing tests of validity, reliability, and classical assumptions. The results indicate that financial knowledge, positive emotions, and store atmosphere have both partial and simultaneous effects on impulse buying behavior. title: The Role of Digital Leadership in Enhancing Data-Driven Instruction and Curriculum Design in Higher Education
text_snippet: The Role of Digital Leadership in Enhancing Data-Driven Instruction and Curriculum Design in Higher Education The integration of digital leadership in the higher education ecosystem is a fundamental prerequisite for strengthening data-driven instructional decision-making. This study aims to explore the optimization of the role of digital leadership in integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and data-driven strategies to improve pedagogical effectiveness and learning outcomes. This study uses a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, participatory observation, and documentation analysis of academic leaders, educators, and educational technology specialists as key informants. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis techniques through a process of data reduction, categorization, and iterative conclusion drawing. The results show that effective digital leadership requires leaders to act as mediators between the technological and pedagogical dimensions, going beyond mere technical mastery. The success of integration depends on a systematic, step-by-step approach and the continuous strengthening of educators' digital competencies, despite the challenges of the digital divide and institutional resistance. title: Teacher Qualities as Predictors of Mathematics Achievement
text_snippet: Teacher Qualities as Predictors of Mathematics Achievement Students’ mathematics performance continues to show considerable variation influenced by internal teacher-related factors, while empirical evidence regarding the roles of teacher self-efficacy, interest, and attitudes remains inconclusive. This condition raises questions about which teacher attributes contribute most significantly to students’ academic achievement. This study aims to analyze the relationships, evaluate the effects, and determine the relative contributions of teachers’ self-efficacy, interest, and attitudes to students’ mathematics achievement. This quantitative study employed a descriptive-correlational design to systematically examine the relationships among the variables. The study involved 40 mathematics teachers and 270 students as research participants. Data were collected through standardized surveys to measure teacher attributes and through documentation of students’ scores to assess academic achievement. The data were analyzed using Pearson’s r correlation to identify the strength and direction of relationships between variables. title: The Influence of Digital Comic Strip Media on Procedural Text Writing Skills in Elementary Schools
text_snippet: The Influence of Digital Comic Strip Media on Procedural Text Writing Skills in Elementary Schools The low skill of writing procedural texts in the Indonesian language subjects in elementary schools. Learning is needed that encourages the development of procedural text writing skills, one of which is through digital comic strip media. The purpose of this study is to analyze the effect of digital comic strip media learning on procedural text writing skills in elementary schools. The method in this study uses a quantitative approach with a one-group pretest-posttest design. The research was conducted at an elementary school in the Wonogiri district with 22 students as subjects. Data collection techniques used were observation and tests. Data analysis techniques included descriptive and inferential statistical analyses, including normality tests and paired-samples t-tests, using SPSS version 16. The results of this study indicate that using this media has a significant positive impact on students' writing skills.
